subject.title: [Bug]: macOS Dashboard window keeps a dead SSH tunnel port after tunnel restart (remote mode)

question: Should the macOS Dashboard handle tunnel endpoint changes by reloading the WebView after reinjecting native auth, or should it expose a live endpoint-update bridge to the running Control UI?
rationale: Both approaches can solve the stale-port bug, but they differ in UX, WebView auth lifecycle, and how much web/native bridge surface becomes a product contract.

options.title: Reload on endpoint change
options.body: Subscribe in the macOS Dashboard path, reinject auth for the new origin, and reload the WebView when the endpoint changes; this is narrower and easier to prove.

options.title: Bridge live endpoint updates
options.body: Add a native-to-web update path so the running Control UI reconnects without a reload, which is smoother but creates a broader bridge contract.

options.title: Defer to tunnel stability work
options.body: Wait for the orphaned-tunnel and web reconnect fixes first, accepting that an open remote Dashboard can stay stuck after a tunnel port change.

recommendation.title: Reload on endpoint change
recommendation.body: Subscribe in the macOS Dashboard path, reinject auth for the new origin, and reload the WebView when the endpoint changes; this is narrower and easier to prove.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the concrete macOS reproduction and are the strongest item-specific routing candidate in the likely-owner list.
